The EU reacted after the yes vote. For example, it suspended negotiations on Switzerland's participation in the education programme **Erasmus+**. Erasmus+ allows students to go on exchanges at universities in Europe.

Parliament searched for a long time for a solution that would implement the constitution without breaching the agreement with the EU. In **December 2016** it decided on the **“light” priority for domestic workers** (Inländervorrang light). It did without quotas. Instead, vacancies in occupations with high unemployment must first be reported to the **job centres**. In this way people who already live in Switzerland are to get a head start.

The supporters felt that immigration was too high and put a strain on, for example, the housing market, transport and the environment. They later criticised the implementation as too weak. The opponents warned of damage to the economy and to relations with the EU. They welcomed the fact that the **bilateral path** was preserved. The question of how Switzerland should regulate immigration remains an important political topic to this day.

gewusst: Fewer than 20,000 votes decided an initiative that shaped Switzerland's relationship with Europe for years.
In 2020 the people rejected the SVP's limitation initiative, which wanted to end the Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons.

teile.einleitung: The Act of Mediation was a constitution that Napoleon Bonaparte gave Switzerland in 1803. It ended the turmoil of the Helvetic Republic and created a Switzerland with 19 cantons. The period up to 1813 is called the Mediation period.
wichtigste: Napoleon Bonaparte handed over the Act of Mediation on 19 February 1803.
Afterwards Switzerland had 19 cantons.
Six cantons were newly created, including Aargau and Ticino.
Valais did not belong to Switzerland during this period.
The Diet (Tagsatzung) was the assembly of the cantonal envoys.
At the top there was a different Landammann of Switzerland every year.
After Napoleon's fall, the Federal Treaty of 1815 followed.

abschnitte.text: After 1798 Switzerland was the **Helvetic Republic**, a unitary state on the French model. There was a lot of conflict and unrest. The French ruler **Napoleon Bonaparte** intervened. On **19 February 1803** he handed over the **Act of Mediation**. “Mediation” means acting as a go-between. So Napoleon presented himself as a mediator between the quarrelling groups.

The Act of Mediation restored the **13 old cantons**. In addition there were **six new cantons**: **St Gallen**, the **Grisons**, **Aargau**, **Thurgau**, **Ticino** and **Vaud**. Together this made **19 cantons**. Many of the new cantons had previously been **subject territories**. **Ticino**, for example, had been ruled by the Confederates and was now a canton with equal rights. Valais, Geneva and Neuchâtel only joined in 1815.

The cantons regained a great deal of independence. They discussed common questions in the **Diet** (Tagsatzung). There envoys of the cantons met and voted according to the instructions of their governments. Six **directorial cantons** took turns each year: **Fribourg, Bern, Solothurn, Basel, Zurich and Lucerne**. The chief magistrate or mayor of that canton became the **Landammann of Switzerland** and ran the affairs.

During this period Switzerland was heavily dependent on **France**. Under the **military capitulation of 1803**, France was allowed to recruit **16,000 men** in Switzerland in peacetime. That is why many Swiss soldiers fought in Napoleon's armies. **Valais** had been a separate republic since 1802 and in 1810 was even **annexed** by France, that is taken over.

In **1813** Napoleon lost a decisive battle and his power collapsed. With that, the Act of Mediation also lost its footing. The cantons negotiated a new order. The **Federal Treaty of 1815** made Switzerland a loose **confederation of states** again. But the six new cantons of 1803 remained.

gewusst: The cantons of Aargau, Thurgau, St Gallen, the Grisons, Ticino and Vaud celebrated their 200th anniversary in 2003.
The Act of Mediation was not drawn up in Switzerland but in Paris.

teile.einleitung: In several Swiss cantons, Landammann is the title of the president of the cantonal government. The office is particularly well known in the Landsgemeinde cantons of Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
wichtigste: The Landammann is the president of the cantonal government.
In Glarus he or she presides over the Landsgemeinde and is elected by it.
The deputy in Glarus is called the Landesstatthalter.
Appenzell Innerrhoden has two Landammänner.
The governing and the “standing still” Landammann take turns.
The state sword is a symbol of the office.

abschnitte.text: The word **Landammann** is an old title for the highest representative of a “Land”, that is a canton. Today, in several cantons, it refers to the **president of the cantonal government**. Besides Glarus and the two Appenzells, the title is also used for example in Uri, Zug and Aargau. In other cantons the office is called president of the government.

In **Glarus** the Landammann is elected by the **Landsgemeinde**. The voters vote in the ring by **show of hands**, that is by raising their hand. The Landammann opens and presides over the Landsgemeinde. At the beginning he or she administers the **oath**: everyone promises to serve the canton. During the Landsgemeinde the Landammann leans on the **state sword**, a symbol of the office.

The deputy of the Glarus Landammann is called the **Landesstatthalter**. He or she is the vice-president of the government and is also elected at the Landsgemeinde. If the Landammann is absent, the Landesstatthalter takes over his or her duties.

In **Appenzell Innerrhoden** there are **two Landammänner**: a **governing** one and a **“standing still”** one. The governing Landammann leads the government, which there is called the **Standeskommission**. The “standing still” Landammann remains a member of the government. Every two years the two swap roles. In this way each of them leads the canton in turn.

gewusst: The title “standing still Landammann” sounds funny, but it only means that he or she is not at the top just now.
Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden are the last two cantons with a Landsgemeinde.

teile.einleitung: A legislative period is the length of time an elected parliament or government is in office. After that there is a new election. In Switzerland a legislative period at federal level lasts four years.
wichtigste: A legislative period is the term of office of an elected parliament or government.
At federal level in Switzerland it lasts four years.
The National Council is re-elected in October, most recently in 2023.
The next federal elections will take place in autumn 2027.
After each new election of parliament, the Federal Council is elected in December for four years.
In most cantons a legislative period also lasts four years, in some five years.
The word comes from the Latin “legislatio”, which means law-making.

abschnitte.text: The **legislative period** is the time between two parliamentary elections. During this time the elected members work in parliament and make laws. At the end they must stand for election again. In this way voters can regularly decide afresh who should represent them.

The **National Council** is elected every four years in October; the last election was in 2023 and the next is in 2027. In most cantons the members of the Council of States are elected at the same time. At the beginning of December the new legislative period begins with the first session. Shortly afterwards the United Federal Assembly elects the **Federal Council** for the next four years.

Cantons and municipalities also have legislative periods. Most cantons elect their parliament and government every four years. Some cantons, for example Geneva and Vaud, have a term of office of five years. Election dates differ between the cantons, which is why there is an election somewhere in Switzerland almost every year.

At the start of each legislative period the Federal Council presents its **legislative planning**. It sets out which goals it wants to achieve over the next four years. Parliament debates this plan and can change it. This way everyone knows which big topics are to be tackled in the coming years.

Other countries also have legislative periods. The German Bundestag is usually elected every four years. The European Parliament has a term of office of five years. In some countries parliament can be dissolved early; in Switzerland this is not provided for at federal level.

begriffe.erklaerung: The law-making power, that is parliament.
The time during which someone holds an office.
An election in which all the seats are filled anew.
The Federal Council's plan for the goals of a legislative period.

gewusst: Until 1931 the term of office of the National Council lasted only three years; since then it has been four years.
Because the Swiss Federal Council cannot be voted out, it stays in office until the end of the legislative period even if there are arguments in parliament.

teile.einleitung: Every car in Switzerland carries a number plate, also called a registration plate or licence plate. The two letters on it reveal in which canton the vehicle is registered.
wichtigste: The two letters show the canton, followed by a number.
Zurich has ZH, the Grisons GR, Nidwalden NW.
TI for Ticino comes from the Italian name Ticino.
VS for Valais comes from the Latin name Vallesia.
At the back you can see the Swiss coat of arms and the cantonal coat of arms.
Normal plates are white with black lettering.

abschnitte.text: A Swiss **number plate** starts with **two letters**. They show in which **canton** the car is registered. They are followed by a **number**. You get the plate from the cantonal **road traffic office**. This means every vehicle can be traced to its keeper.

Many abbreviations are easy to guess: **ZH** stands for Zurich, **GR** for the Grisons (Graubünden), **NW** for Nidwalden, that is Nid and Walden. Some come from another language. **TI** comes from the Italian name **Ticino**, because Italian is spoken in Ticino. **FR** comes from the French **Fribourg**; in Fribourg people speak French and German. **VS** stands for Valais (Wallis), in Latin **Vallesia** and in French Valais.

abschnitte.titel: Coats of arms on the plate
abschnitte.text: On the **rear plate** you can see two coats of arms next to the number: the **Swiss coat of arms** and the **cantonal coat of arms**. So you can also recognise the canton from the picture. The front plate only carries the letters and the number. Abroad, a **CH** sticker also shows that the car comes from Switzerland.

Normal car plates are **white with black lettering**. This makes them easy to read. Other vehicles have other colours: mopeds carry small **yellow** plates. Agricultural vehicles such as tractors have **green** plates. Working machines carry **blue** plates.

gewusst: CH stands for “Confoederatio Helvetica”, the Latin name of Switzerland.
In Switzerland the number plate belongs to the keeper and not to the car: with a new car you can keep the old number.

teile.einleitung: The Landsgemeinde is an open-air assembly at which the voters of a canton vote and elect together. Instead of putting a paper into a ballot box, everyone raises their hand. Today the Landsgemeinde only exists in the cantons of Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
wichtigste: The Landsgemeinde is the oldest form of direct democracy in Switzerland.
Today it only exists in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
Voting is done by raising hands in a large square.
The Landsgemeinde in Appenzell takes place on the last Sunday in April.
The Glarus Landsgemeinde meets on the first Sunday in May.
Other cantons such as Nidwalden, Obwalden and Appenzell Ausserrhoden abolished it in the 1990s.
In 2007 Glarus was the first canton to introduce a voting age of 16, and it did so at the Landsgemeinde.

abschnitte.text: The **Landsgemeinde** is the assembly of all the voters of a canton. It takes place once a year in a large square, the **ring**. There people vote on new laws, taxes and spending. In addition, the government and judges are elected.

Voting is done by raising hands; this is called a **show of hands**. The Landammann, that is the head of the cantonal government, estimates from a stage which side has more hands. If the result is close, the vote is repeated until it is clear. Anyone may also step forward and make a speech in front of everyone.

Landsgemeinden already existed in the Middle Ages in several places in Central and Eastern Switzerland. In Glarus the Landsgemeinde has been documented since the 14th century. Uri, Schwyz, Zug, Obwalden, Nidwalden and Appenzell Ausserrhoden also used to have a Landsgemeinde. One by one these cantons replaced it with voting at the ballot box, most recently Obwalden in 1998.

For a long time only men were allowed to take part in the Landsgemeinde. In Appenzell Innerrhoden the men used to carry a **sabre** or sword as proof of identity. Only in 1990 did the Federal Supreme Court decide that women in Appenzell Innerrhoden could also have a say at cantonal level. Since 1991 women and men have stood together in the ring there.

The Landsgemeinde in **Appenzell** takes place on the Landsgemeinde square in the middle of the village. The people of Glarus gather on the Zaunplatz in Glarus. In 2006 the Glarus Landsgemeinde decided to greatly reduce the number of municipalities; since 2011 there have been only three. Both Landsgemeinden attract many visitors from Switzerland and abroad every year.

begriffe.erklaerung: The square where the voters stand at the Landsgemeinde.
The president of the cantonal government in some cantons.
A vote in which you raise your hand and the larger side wins.
People who are allowed to vote and elect.

gewusst: At the Glarus Landsgemeinde even 16-year-olds may vote; in 2007 this did not exist in any other canton.
At the Landsgemeinde there is no secret ballot, because everyone can see how you raise your hand.

teile.einleitung: The Responsible Business Initiative (in German “Konzernverantwortungsinitiative”) wanted Swiss companies to respect human rights and environmental standards abroad too and to be liable for damage. On 29 November 2020 a narrow majority of the people did vote yes, but the initiative failed because it did not win a majority of the cantons.
wichtigste: The vote took place on 29 November 2020.
50.7 per cent of voters said yes.
The initiative failed because the majority of the cantons said no.
Only 8.5 cantonal votes were in favour, 14.5 against.
Behind the initiative were aid organisations, human rights groups and environmental organisations.
An indirect counter-proposal with reporting duties came into force.

abschnitte.text: Companies based in Switzerland were to respect **human rights** and **environmental standards** **abroad** too. In the event of violations they would have been **liable** for damage, including for companies they control. The initiative was launched by an alliance of over a hundred organisations, including many **aid organisations**. In October 2016 they handed in a good 120,000 signatures.

abschnitte.titel: Majority of the people, but not of the cantons
abschnitte.text: A popular initiative needs a **majority of the people** and a **majority of the cantons**, that is the majority of voters and the majority of the cantons. On 29 November 2020, **50.7 per cent** voted yes. The cantons, however, rejected it: only **8.5 cantonal votes** were in favour, **14.5** against. A majority of the cantons would have needed at least 12. Turnout was around 47 per cent.

It is very rare for a popular initiative to fail because of the cantons despite a majority of the people. Before that, it had only happened to the **tenant and consumer protection initiative** of 1955. The Responsible Business Initiative was therefore only the second. The result shows how the majority of the cantons strengthens the small cantons.

The campaign was one of the most elaborate of recent years. A well-known face was the former Ticino member of the Council of States **Dick Marty** of the FDP, co-president of the initiative committee. The supporters wanted to hold companies to account. The opponents, including business associations and the Federal Council, warned of disadvantages for Swiss companies and of difficult court cases.

Parliament had passed an **indirect counter-proposal**. It came into force after the no to the initiative. Since then, large companies have had to report on **human rights** and the **environment**. In some areas, for example child labour, additional due diligence duties apply. However, the companies do not have to be liable in the way the initiative had demanded.

gewusst: In the cantonal votes, the cantons of Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden each count as half, which is why there are results like 8.5 to 14.5.
There are 23 cantonal votes in total, so a majority of the cantons needs at least 12.

teile.einleitung: Freedom of the media means that newspapers, radio, television and online media may report freely. The state may not dictate their content to them. Independent media are important for democracy.
wichtigste: The media are regarded as the fourth power in the state.
The Federal Constitution guarantees radio and television independence in designing their programmes.
Anyone affected by false statements of fact can demand a right of reply.
OFCOM supervises radio and television without dictating programmes.
Complaints against broadcasts are decided by the UBI.
Advertising and journalism must be clearly separated.
The media package was rejected by the people in February 2022.

abschnitte.text: In the state there are three powers: parliament, the government and the courts. Independent media are often called the **fourth power** (or fourth estate). They inform the public, put events into context and uncover **abuses**. In this way they keep a check on government, parliament and the courts. To be able to do this, they must be allowed to report freely. That is why the Federal Constitution protects **freedom of the media**.

**Article 93** of the Federal Constitution states that radio and television are **independent** and design their programmes themselves. The state may not dictate their content. Nevertheless there is supervision. The **Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM)** checks, for example, whether broadcasters comply with their **licences**. It may not interfere with the content of programmes.

Anyone who thinks a broadcast is unfair can first turn to an **ombudsman's office**. It mediates. After that the **Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television (UBI)** decides. It examines, for example, whether a broadcast has breached the **requirement of fair and accurate reporting**. Its decisions can be appealed to the Federal Supreme Court. Anyone directly affected by a presentation of facts in a medium can also demand a **right of reply**. In it, their own view of the facts is published in the same medium.

Media should clearly separate **advertising** and **editorial content**. Whoever pays must not decide what the journalists write. Hidden advertising that looks like a normal article is called **surreptitious advertising**. It deceives the public and endangers the independence of the media. That is why advertising is usually labelled with words such as “advertisement” or “sponsored”.

For democracy it is important that there are many different media. When a few companies own many media, this is called **media concentration**. Then the variety of voices decreases, which can weaken the forming of opinions. The Confederation wanted to give the media more support. But on **13 February 2022** voters rejected the **media package** with around 55 per cent voting no. Supporters wanted to safeguard diversity this way; opponents feared dependence on the state.

gewusst: The right of reply is regulated in the Swiss Civil Code.
Censorship is expressly forbidden in the Swiss Federal Constitution.

teile.einleitung: A list combination is formed when two or more parties link their electoral lists. In this way they cooperate in the distribution of seats. In Switzerland list combinations play a big role above all in the National Council elections.
wichtigste: In a list combination, two or more parties link their lists.
The votes of the linked lists are added together in the first distribution of seats.
This means fewer votes are lost that would otherwise not be enough for a seat.
List combinations exist in proportional elections, for example for the National Council.
Usually parties that think alike politically link up.
Within a party there are also sub-list combinations, for example between the main party and its youth party.
List combinations must be registered before the election.

abschnitte.text: In a **list combination** parties join forces for an election. But they still stand with their own lists and their own candidates. The link only has an effect when the seats are calculated. The ballot paper shows which lists a list is linked with.

When the seats are distributed, the votes of all the linked lists are first added together. The group is treated like a single large list. Afterwards the seats won are distributed within the group among the individual parties. For the National Council the **Hagenbach-Bischoff** method is used for the distribution.

Imagine two small parties each have a few thousand votes, but neither alone reaches enough for a seat. If they link their lists, their votes together may be enough for a **remaining seat**. This seat then goes to the party in the group with more votes. Without the link, the votes of both parties would have had no effect.

Within a list combination there can also be **sub-list combinations**. Often a party links its main list with the list of its youth party or a list from a particular region. First the seat is distributed within the group, then within the sub-list. In this way the votes stay as far as possible within the same political family.

List combinations are controversial. Supporters say that fewer votes are lost and small parties have a chance. Critics feel that voters often do not know whom their vote helps in the end. That is why the media report in detail before every election on which parties have linked up.

begriffe.erklaerung: The calculation of how many seats each party receives.
A seat that is still left over after the first distribution.

gewusst: A list combination can mean that a party gets a seat even though it has fewer votes than another party without a link.
